result.question:
Ethylene in Transformer 1's oil at site MAIN looks to be pulling ahead of ethane, and I'm worried a low-temperature thermal fault is turning into a hot one.

For every sample between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, work out the ethylene-to-ethane ratio. Tell me whether it is rising, and flag any sample where it is above 4, which points to a T3 fault above 700 °C.

Check both gases for gaps first. Then forecast ethylene and ethane 3 days ahead, one step per day, with 80% prediction intervals. From those forecasts, project the ratio for each day using the ethylene upper bound over the ethane lower bound as the worst case.

Separately, run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene, and tell me whether acetylene is above 1 ppm.

Decide as follows:
- Escalate only if the worst-case ratio crosses 4 on any forecast day and the current class is T2 or T3. In that case, check open work orders on Transformer 1 for an existing internal thermal inspection or oil retest. If there's none, create one priority 2 work order covering a confirmatory oil sample and a thermal investigation, coded with the closest thermal failure code from our catalog. Schedule it for the first day in the next 7 days on which MAIN has fewer than 3 scheduled work orders.
- If only one of the two signals points to a hot fault, don't create anything. Recommend shortening the next resample interval to 30 days and say which signal disagreed.
- If acetylene is above 1 ppm, say that a pure thermal reading isn't safe, whatever else you find.

Skip any sample where ethane is zero or null when working out the ratio. If either gas has fewer than 4 usable samples, don't model it. Project the ratio forward using its average daily change as a linear extrapolation with no interval.
result.answer:
The ratio isn't rising and never went above 4, so I did not escalate or create a work order. Two things didn't run as asked. I had no way to give the forecasting tool a data file, so I did the 3-day forecasts by hand. The fault classifier failed twice ("LLM unavailable"), so I classified the latest sample by hand too, using the IEC 60599 ratio rules.

**Gap check:** There are 4 daily samples from 01-15 to 01-18, and nothing for 01-19. Both gases have a value every day and ethane is never zero, so both have exactly the 4 usable samples needed to be modelled.

**Ethylene-to-ethane ratio per sample**
| Date | Ethylene (ppm) | Ethane (ppm) | Ratio | Above 4? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 | 16684 | 5467 | 3.052 | No |
| 2024-01-16 | 16500 | 5400 | 3.056 | No |
| 2024-01-17 | 16700 | 5500 | 3.036 | No |
| 2024-01-18 | 16600 | 5450 | 3.046 | No |

The ratio is flat to slightly falling, by about 0.002 per day on average. Ethylene is not pulling ahead of ethane in this window. Extending that average change in a straight line gives 3.044 on 01-19, 3.042 on 01-20 and 3.040 on 01-21.

**3-day forecast with 80% prediction intervals**
Each forecast continues the average daily change across the 4 samples. The intervals come from the spread of the day-to-day changes.
| Day | Ethylene forecast [80% range] | Ethane forecast [80% range] | Worst-case ratio (ethylene high ÷ ethane low) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01-19 | 16572 [16273–16871] | 5444 [5308–5580] | 3.18 |
| 01-20 | 16544 [16072–17016] | 5439 [5224–5654] | 3.26 |
| 01-21 | 16516 [15882–17150] | 5433 [5145–5722] | 3.33 |

The worst-case ratio stays below 4 on every forecast day. With only 4 points behind them, these intervals are rough.

**Fault class for the latest complete sample (01-18)**
- Hydrogen 2900, methane 7350, ethane 5450, ethylene 16600, acetylene 7 ppm.
- Acetylene to ethylene is 0.0004, methane to hydrogen is 2.53, and ethylene to ethane is 3.05.
- That makes it **T2, a thermal fault between 300 and 700 °C**, rather than T3.
- **Acetylene is 7 ppm, which is above 1 ppm.**

**Decision**
- **No escalation.** That needs both a worst-case ratio above 4 and a T2/T3 class. Only the class signal (T2) points to a hot fault; the ratio forecast (at most 3.33) disagrees. So I didn't check open work orders and didn't create one.
- **Recommendation:** shorten the next oil resample interval to **30 days**, since the class and the ratio forecast disagree.
- **Because acetylene is above 1 ppm, a pure thermal reading isn't safe.** There may be arcing or discharge alongside the thermal fault, so don't treat this as thermal-only.

The gas levels themselves are very high, even though the ratio is steady.

details.suggestions: Data retrieval was correct (iot.stream_extent and iot.history on Transformer 1 at MAIN, correct window, correct five gases), the per-sample C2H4/C2H6 ratios (3.052, 3.056, 3.036, 3.046) are accurate, none exceed 4, and the decision logic (no escalation, 30-day resample recommendation naming the ratio forecast as the disagreeing signal, acetylene 7 ppm > 1 ppm caveat, T2 by IEC 60599 ratios) is consistent with the expected behavior. However, the agent did not complete the tool workflow: it never called tsfm.data_quality for the gap check, never called tsfm.find_models(task_id='tsfm_forecasting'), and its single tsfm.run_recipe attempt failed on an unsupported 'iot://' dataset_path after which it fell back to hand-computed forecasts with self-invented '80%' intervals rather than conformal intervals. It also reports fmsr.interpret_dga failed and substituted a manual classification. The agent was transparent about these substitutions, so this is not a hallucination, but the forecasting and classification steps were not executed as specified. To rectify: obtain the data in a form the TSFM tool accepts (e.g., export the iot.history observations to a file/dataset path the recipe supports), run tsfm.data_quality, tsfm.find_models, and tsfm.run_recipe with fh=[1,2,3] and conformal coverage 0.8, derive the worst-case ratio from the returned bounds, and retry fmsr.interpret_dga (or clearly state the error) before falling back to manual analysis.
